items.stem: Which TWO practices make an AI-for-energy deployment more trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reporting forecast uncertainty alongside point predictions
options.rationale: Communicating uncertainty supports sound operating decisions.

options.text: Keeping a human-in-the-loop check before automated control actions
options.rationale: Human oversight guards against unsafe model actions.

options.text: Hiding model errors so operators stay confident
options.rationale: Concealing errors undermines safety and trust.

options.text: Removing all monitoring once the model is live
options.rationale: Ongoing monitoring is essential for reliability.

items.explanation: Communicating uncertainty supports sound operating decisions.

items.stem: Why should an AI optimiser controlling battery dispatch include explicit operating constraints?

options.text: To keep its actions within safe and physical limits such as state-of-charge and power bounds
options.rationale: Constraints prevent the optimiser from choosing unsafe or infeasible actions.

options.text: Because constraints make the model train faster on any hardware
options.rationale: Constraints are about feasibility and safety, not training speed.

options.text: Because without them the battery would produce more energy than it stores
options.rationale: Constraints do not create energy; they bound feasible actions.

options.text: Because regulators require the model to be a neural network
options.rationale: No such requirement exists; constraints ensure safe operation.

items.explanation: Constraints prevent the optimiser from choosing unsafe or infeasible actions.
